kata.name: kata cor-strategy-rules above the floor: a legacy Chain-of-Responsibility + Strategy dispatcher as a 7-rule table — the unique band is behaviour-preserving structural redundancy
kata.series_report: fixtures/katas/cor-strategy-rules/README.md (pre-registered); docs/ref/ploeh-grounding.md section 6 candidate 1; P8 precedent fixtures/rule_lens/README.md
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: authored-table reverse-engineering transfer — unique detections only on structural redundancy (an unsampled guard gap, a dead handler, a derivable branch); every behaviour-changing fault is caught by the scripted dispatch sample, so no detection-rate win is claimed

expected.detail: a handler guard leaves a request class unhandled (a missing or narrowed chain handler); the rule lens witnesses it as `underconstraint` (hypothesized) naming the uncovered class
a handler is dead under chain order because an earlier guard subsumes it; the rule lens witnesses it as `redundant` (executed) naming the dead handler and its covering predecessors
a strategy branch is derivable: its region equals the intersection of two other rules; the rule lens witnesses it as `redundant` (executed) naming the branch and both factors
the table declares `DeclaredDisjoint` while two guards intersect; the rule lens witnesses it as one `violation` (executed) per intersecting pair and shared input
a handler selects the wrong strategy; the rule surface carries the action token without semantics, so the lens cannot express it — the honest boundary of the reverse-engineering transfer

floor control — at the two-handler/4-input chain the scripted dispatch test enumerates the whole input space and catches every injected fault; the kata must show zero unique detections here (kata-6 triviality-floor analog)

comparison.conventional_baseline: The scripted dispatch sample asserts seven request cases above the floor — one per handler path — resolved under the chain's `PriorityOrder`; it catches the deleted fallback, the widened payout guard and the declared-disjointness claim, and it is blind to the narrowed fallback's unsampled batch half, to a duplicate handler, and to a derivable branch whose action matches the chain.
unique_detections: 02-chain-gap-fallback-narrow: `admin` requests on the `batch` channel at amounts 0 and 50 are covered by no handler; the frozen sample checks only `admin/0/web`, so its guard assertion passes
03-shadow-duplicate-payout: `payout_guard_repeat` is dead under `PriorityOrder`, reduced by `payout_guard`; the scripted sample resolves every case identically

05-derivable-strategy-branch: `payout_high_value` is derivable — its region equals `payout_guard` intersect `large_amount` — and it carries the same action, so dispatch behaviour is unchanged and the sample cannot see it

baseline.artifact: prototype/cor_strategy_rules_baseline.py sha256:16e24552fbc5ed45ab8e5083225e99e3e4dc8eca34706b95467f4dc30a26a5e2 (scripted dispatch sample: 7 request cases above the floor, one per handler path, plus the whole 4-input space at the near-floor control, each resolved under the document's declared policy)

expressibility_gap.invariant: the selected strategy is the handler's semantic output
expressibility_gap.why: rule_presentation actions are opaque tokens: a handler whose guard is right but whose action selects the wrong strategy (fault 07) produces no structural finding, and the lens must stay silent rather than guess

expressibility_gap.invariant: a dispatcher's chain order is policy, not law
expressibility_gap.why: under a priority policy an intersection is resolved by order and never reported; the same regions under DeclaredDisjoint are violations. The lens can only report what the document declares, so a table whose policy is unstated cannot be judged for overlap (Decision 1/3).

discrepancies: Scope: the table is authored for this kata. The P8 precedent (fixtures/rule_lens/README.md) stands — an authored rule table is a commodity; the three unique detections are behaviour-preserving structural redundancy on a guard set reconstructed from legacy code. This is reverse-engineering transfer, not a detection-rate win over a dispatch suite.

Conditionality: the unique count is relative to the committed 7-case sample. A denser sample (an admin/batch case, or a region-partition assertion) would catch fault 02 and the derivable insertion, so the matrix is conditional on the frozen suite, recorded rather than rounded.
procedure: 1. The legacy dispatcher's chain (seven handler guards in order, each action naming handler and strategy), its seven injected faults, the scripted dispatch sample and the frozen expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/cor-strategy-rules/ before the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/cor_strategy_rules_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: seven request cases, one per handler path, resolved under the chain's declared policy and compared with the frozen expected action.

3. The probe arm ran `catherine rules` over the declared finite domain (5 kinds x 3 amounts x 2 channels = 30 inputs, within the 64-candidate budget) on the clean table and on the same seven fault documents; run.findings is the CLI's verbatim output.
4. A fault is caught only when an arm's output evidences it; unique detections are the lens findings on faults the scripted sample missed (the rule-lens P8 comparison procedure, unchanged).
5. The near-floor control ran first and self-negated (0 unique detections at two handlers over 4 inputs), so the above-floor band is read against a self-negating floor.
6. The verdict follows harness::derive_probe_verdict: unique with an executed baseline arm = survived, scoped to the classes actually instanced.
